name: Smart Reviews Display – Display Google, yelp and WordPress reviews
author: Mishal Fatima

sections.description:
Smart Reviews Display lets you showcase reviews from multiple sources including WordPress.org, Yelp, and Google Reviews. Choose from responsive grid (masonry), list, or carousel displays with full reviewer details and smart caching.

Key Features:
– Multiple Review Sources: WordPress.org plugins/themes, Yelp business reviews, Google Places reviews
– Responsive Layouts: Masonry grid, list, and carousel with 60% container width
– Smart Management: Dashboard with add/edit/delete review displays, internal vs display titles
– Rich Content: Avatars, star ratings, descriptions, aggregate ratings, and contextual fields
– ID-Based Shortcodes: Simple [smart_reviews id="123"] format that auto-updates
– Gutenberg Blocks: Full block editor support with live preview
– Smart Caching: Configurable cache management and TTL controls
– Lightweight: No external dependencies, optimized CSS/JS

Usage

Dashboard Management

  1. Go to Smart Reviews Display → Dashboard
  2. Click “Add New Review Display” to create a new configuration
  3. Fill in the form:
    • Internal Title: For backend management (e.g., “WooCommerce Reviews”)
    • Display Title: Shown on frontend (e.g., “What our customers say”)
    • Description: Optional description text
    • Review Source: WordPress.org, Yelp, or Google Reviews
    • Slug/ID: Plugin slug, Yelp business ID, or Google Place ID
    • Type: Plugin/Theme (WordPress.org only), Business (Yelp), Place (Google)
    • Layout: Grid (masonry), List, or Carousel
    • Display Options: Show title, show aggregate rating
  4. Save and use the generated shortcode or block

Block

Search for “Smart Reviews” in the block editor. You can either:
– Use ID: Select a saved review display by ID
– Configure Manually: Set all options directly in the block

Shortcode

New ID-based format (recommended):
[smart_reviews id="123"]

Legacy format (still supported):
[smart_reviews slug="wordpress-seo" type="plugin" limit="6" minrating="0" layout="grid" title="What users say"]

Yelp example:
[smart_reviews source="yelp" business_id="your-business-id" type="business" layout="grid"]

Google Reviews example:
[smart_reviews source="google" place_id="your-place-id" type="place" layout="carousel"]

Attributes:
– id (int) Review display ID from dashboard (recommended)
– source (wporg|yelp|google) Review source
– slug (string) WordPress.org plugin/theme slug
– business_id (string) Yelp business ID
– place_id (string) Google Place ID
– type (plugin|theme|business|place) Contextual based on source
– limit (int, 1–20) Number of reviews to show
– minrating (int, 0–5) Minimum rating filter
– layout (grid|list|carousel) Display layout
– title (string) Display title
– description (string) Description text
– show_title (0|1) Show title on frontend
– show_aggregate (0|1) Show aggregate rating
sections.installation:
1. Upload the smart-reviews-display folder to wp-content/plugins/, or install via Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate through the “Plugins” screen.
  3. Go to Smart Reviews Display → Dashboard to manage review displays.
  4. Add new review displays or use existing ones with blocks/shortcodes.
sections.faq:
What review sources are supported?

WordPress.org (plugins/themes), Yelp business reviews, and Google Places reviews.

How do I get started quickly?

Use the new ID-based shortcode [smart_reviews id="123"] after creating a review display in the dashboard.

Can I show aggregate ratings?

Yes, for WordPress.org plugins and all external sources (Yelp, Google). Themes don’t have aggregate ratings on WordPress.org.

How often are reviews updated?

Reviews are cached with transients. Control TTL and clear cache in Smart Reviews Display → Cache Management.

Can I customize the appearance?

Yes. The plugin uses 60% container width with responsive masonry grid, list, and carousel layouts. Override with custom CSS.

What’s the difference between Internal Title and Display Title?

Internal Title is for backend management only. Display Title appears on the frontend (optional).

Do I need API keys for Yelp/Google?

Yes, you’ll need to configure Yelp Fusion API and Google Places API keys in the settings.
